title: The Projection Atlas
summary: One world, three perspectives. A visual comparison of how map projections reshape geography.
hero_alt: World map in the Equal Earth projection with countries in muted greens and a fine graticule
question: How does the choice of a coordinate reference system change the appearance and interpretation of a world map?
study_area: Global, using 1:110m Natural Earth country boundaries.
outcome: A matched set of maps makes projection distortion visible and connects each CRS to appropriate cartographic uses.
role: Demonstration workflow: data preparation, CRS transformation, cartographic design, and web export with Python.

methods.title: Read & validate
methods.text: Load Natural Earth country polygons and confirm the geographic source CRS, EPSG:4326.

methods.title: Transform
methods.text: Reproject the same source geometries to Equal Earth, Web Mercator, and Robinson using GeoPandas and PyProj.

methods.title: Design
methods.text: Apply a consistent visual hierarchy, graticule, ocean treatment, and projection-specific extent.

methods.title: Export
methods.text: Render high-resolution maps with Matplotlib and produce responsive WebP assets for the site.

maps.title: Equal Earth
maps.alt: World countries mapped with the Equal Earth projection
maps.caption: An equal-area world view with a familiar, balanced overall shape.

maps.title: Web Mercator
maps.alt: World countries mapped with the Web Mercator projection, truncated near the poles
maps.caption: Conformal and useful for web navigation, but high-latitude areas are greatly exaggerated.

maps.title: Robinson
maps.alt: World countries mapped with the Robinson projection
maps.caption: A compromise projection designed for a visually pleasing world map rather than preserving one metric property.
